newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Index shows strong start in '97.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Index shows strong start in '97.

text.p: Members of the National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit reported on Monday a gain of 5.3 points in overall business conditions in southeastern Michigan's industrial economy.
The index for January was 58.2 compared to 52.9 in December. A year earlier, the index stood at 59.6.
Members were surveyed by Comerica Bank.

The January production index stood at 62.2, up from 51.5 in December. Other elements of the index were as follows: new orders, 58.9, up from 52.3; inventories, 43.3, down from 45.9; employment, 60.9, up from 53.6; vendor performance, 58.7, up from 51.6; and prices, 59.8, up from 47.7.
"Judging from strength in production and new order activity, the regional industrial economy has begun 1997 on a very strong note," said David Littmann, senior economist with Comerica Bank.

The index is a seasonally adjusted weighted average measure of new orders and production activity, along with employment, inventories and the promptness of supplier company deliveries. It ranges from 0 to 100. A composite index below 50 generally means conditions are deteriorating. Levels above 50 denote expansion.
